                                  lighter in colour the thicker it gets.
                                              It doesn’t flow or move much, but breaks a little at the edges.

                             This is a firing schedule I found mentioned in a few forums and on digital fire, while researching pinholes.


                        The drop and hold allows the glaze to settle and for any trapped gasses escape and the slow cool is designed to allow the surface to heal.


                         does it? I don't know. I'm using this as my main firing schedule from now on so we'll see. I will report back.


                                 interestingly I thought a slow cool would use loads of electricity (i dont know why), it used 1kWh my kiln is only little and is 3kW.
